text.p: The United States is considering using military forces in the Adriatic to evacutate Americans from Albania because of worsening instability in the Balkan country, a White House spokesman said on Thursday.

"That's one of the things they're looking at now -- how they might move people out given the fact that it looks as though commericial flights have been suspended," spokesman David Johnson told reporters.

Violence sparked by the collapse of investment schemes has spread from southern Albania toward the capital Tirana. International airline officials reported on Thursday that Tirana airport was closed, hampering the evacuation of some foreign embassy staff and families.
The U.S. State Department said on Wednesday it was ordering 160 embassy employees and their dependents to leave by regular or charter flights. Another 2,000 Americans were urged to go.
Johnson said Americans were not a target in the spreading disorder, but simply faced a danger of "being in the wrong place at the wrong time."

The United States has powerful naval forces off the coast of Albania, including a carrier task force led by the Theodore Roosevelt which includes Marine landing teams that would presumably carry out any evacuation.
